note: SHARED validation fixtures (#3485) — run by BOTH the TypeScript validator (generalNode.ts) and the Rust one (bsc ui validate). schema.ts has long CLAIMED 'a spec that passes here passes there'; with two independent implementations in different languages that claim has to be TESTED, because two validators drifting apart is worse than one — callers trust the agreement precisely where it is most likely to quietly break. Each case: `node` is validated, `count` is the exact number of errors expected, and every string in `contains` must appear in some error. Hand-authored (unlike primitives.json, which is generated).

cases.name: a complete node validates clean
an unknown primitive is rejected and named
a non-object is not a node
a node with no type is rejected
a missing required prop is reported with its name
an out-of-union enum value lists the allowed set
a scalar type mismatch is caught
an absent optional prop is fine — the component default applies
unknown props are NOT flagged on a passthrough primitive
unknown props ARE flagged on a non-passthrough primitive
a space prop accepts a rung name or a number
a handler must be an action NAME, never a literal value
a handler given as an action name is accepted
node-level children is sugar for the children prop
children written as a prop validates identically
plain text is a legitimate children value
children entries that are neither nodes nor text are rejected
recursion reports the failing path inside children
array props are checked to the CONTAINER only — wrong container is caught
array CONTENTS are deliberately unvalidated — the documented gap
